correctness.rationale: Kernel stabilization gives injectivity of every power on the algebraic range of the stabilizing power. Lifts of the same vector inside that range are unique and therefore coherent, with near-minimal finite-index norm control. The reverse inequality follows from infimum minimality. The proof handles absent lifts, zero vectors, zero ascent, infinite growth, and strict radial thresholds. The triangular multiplication-operator example is verified by exact integration and the Riesz representation theorem; no computational assumptions are needed.
